Imagine it’s 3:00 AM. Your pager goes off. The dashboard shows a 100% CPU spike on your primary database, followed by a total service outage. You look at the logs and see a weird pattern: the traffic didn't actually increase, but suddenly every single request started failing at the exact same millisecond.
You’ve just been trampled by the Thundering Herd.

articles.author: Sourav Mahato
articles.description:
Recently I started learning Docker and trying to understand how it actually works behind the scenes. How Docker Engine works, how containers are isolated, and why it is so useful in real development and deployment.
Docker solved one of my biggest pain points. I use Linux, especially openSUSE. A few months ago, I even made a post about PostgreSQL installation issues because many packages don’t properly support openSUSE. It was frustrating.
But with one Docker command, I can run PostgreSQL or almost any database without worrying about OS-level issues. That single thing made me love Docker even more.
For me, learning Docker didn’t feel very difficult because I am already familiar with virtual machines. Containers feel similar to VMs, but they are much more lightweight, resource-efficient, and practical for daily development.
Still learning, but honestly enjoying the process a lot.
articles.title: Docker solved my pain point on My Linux desktop....

articles.author: Sahil Rana
articles.description:
The beginning of a new year is always a powerful moment for reflection, clarity, and renewed motivation. As Sahil Rana, a Full Stack Developer, I see the new year as an opportunity to reset goals, sharpen skills, and continue building meaningful digital solutions.
Reflecting on the Past Year
The past year has been a journey filled with learning, growth, and hands-on problem solving. Working across frontend and backend development allowed me to strengthen my understanding of scalable architectures, performance optimization, and clean, maintainable code. Every project—whether large or small—helped me grow not only as a developer but also as a professional who values accountability, communication, and long-term solutions.
Vision for the New Year
Building high-quality, performance-driven web applications
Writing clean, reusable, and scalable code
Staying aligned with modern technologies and best practices
Delivering solutions that genuinely solve business problems
Technology continues to evolve rapidly, and staying adaptable and curious remains a core part of my approach. This year, I aim to work on more impactful projects that combine strong engineering with thoughtful user experience.
Gratitude and Growth
I am deeply grateful to the clients, teams, and collaborators who trusted me with their projects. Your feedback and collaboration have played a major role in shaping my journey. Moving forward, I look forward to new opportunities, meaningful collaborations, and challenges that push me to grow further as Sahil Rana, Full Stack Developer.
Looking Ahead
The new year is not just about resolutions—it’s about consistency, discipline, and progress. I’m excited to continue this journey with a strong focus on learning, innovation, and delivering reliable digital experiences.
Here’s to a year of growth, purpose, and building things that truly matter.
Happy New Year!
articles.title: New Year Reflections and Goals by Sahil Rana | Full Stack Developer
